fields.regle: Le relatif sujet remplace le sujet : who pour les personnes, which pour les choses, that pour les deux. On ne redouble jamais le sujet — « the woman who lives », jamais « the woman who she lives ».

exercises.prompt: Relie en une phrase : The woman lives next door. She is a surgeon.

accepted: The woman who lives next door is a surgeon
The woman that lives next door is a surgeon

hints: Le relatif prend la place de « she ».

exercises.prompt: Relie en une phrase : The machine broke down. It cost a fortune.

accepted: The machine which broke down cost a fortune
The machine that broke down cost a fortune

hints: Une chose : which ou that, jamais who.

exercises.prompt: Relie en une phrase : I know a photographer. He works for the council.

accepted: I know a photographer who works for the council
I know a photographer that works for the council

hints: Le verbe reste conjugué avec l'antécédent.

exercises.prompt: The people ___ work on the harbour know every tide.

accepted: who
that

exercises.prompt: This is the report ___ explains the delay.

accepted: which
that

exercises.source: The engineer designed the bridge. She is famous.
exercises.prompt: Fais-en une seule phrase avec un relatif.

accepted: The engineer who designed the bridge is famous
The engineer that designed the bridge is famous

hints: La relative s'insère juste après l'antécédent.

exercises.source: The man who he called me was from the bank.
exercises.prompt: Corrige la phrase.

accepted: The man who called me was from the bank
The man that called me was from the bank

hints: « who » est déjà le sujet : « he » est en trop.

exercises.prompt: The train ___ leaves at six is usually late.

accepted: that

fields.regle: Quand le relatif est complément d'objet, on peut l'omettre : « the book (that) I read ». Quand il est sujet, jamais : « the book that fell » garde son relatif.

exercises.prompt: Relie sans employer de relatif : The film was disappointing. We watched it last night.

accepted: The film we watched last night was disappointing

hints: Le relatif était complément : on peut le supprimer.

exercises.prompt: Relie sans employer de relatif : The woman is my line manager. You met her yesterday.

accepted: The woman you met yesterday is my line manager

hints: Pas de « her » après « met » : la place du relatif effacé reste vide.

exercises.prompt: Relie sans employer de relatif : Everything went wrong. He touched it.

accepted: Everything he touched went wrong

exercises.prompt: The invoice ___ arrived this morning is wrong.

accepted: that
which

hints: Ici le relatif est sujet : impossible de l'omettre.

exercises.prompt: Is that the flat you ___ me about last week? (tell)

accepted: told

hints: Le relatif complément a disparu, le reste ne change pas.

exercises.source: The email that I sent on Friday has not been answered.
exercises.prompt: Réécris la phrase en supprimant le relatif.

accepted: The email I sent on Friday has not been answered

exercises.source: The colleague sits opposite me is Welsh.
exercises.prompt: Corrige la phrase.

accepted: The colleague who sits opposite me is Welsh
The colleague that sits opposite me is Welsh

hints: Le relatif est sujet : on ne peut pas l'omettre.

exercises.prompt: Laquelle est correcte ?

accepted: The person I spoke to was helpful

distractors: The person spoke to me was helpful
The person who I spoke to him was helpful
The person which I spoke to was helpful
hints: Relatif complément, donc omissible ; une personne n'est jamais « which ».

fields.regle: whose marque la possession, whom est le complément (registre soutenu), where renvoie à un lieu : « the man whose car », « the woman whom I met », « the office where I work ».

exercises.prompt: Relie : I met a designer. Her studio is in Stokes Croft.

accepted: I met a designer whose studio is in Stokes Croft

hints: « her » devient whose, collé au nom possédé.

exercises.prompt: Relie : This is the café. We first met there.

accepted: This is the café where we first met

hints: Un lieu : where, et « there » disparaît.

exercises.prompt: Relie en registre soutenu : The candidate was excellent. We interviewed her on Tuesday.

accepted: The candidate whom we interviewed on Tuesday was excellent

hints: Complément de personne, registre écrit : whom.

exercises.prompt: The supplier ___ contract expires in June has gone quiet.

accepted: whose

exercises.prompt: I still remember the building ___ the studio used to be.

accepted: where

exercises.source: That is the architect. His drawings are in the museum.
exercises.prompt: Fais-en une seule phrase.

accepted: That is the architect whose drawings are in the museum

exercises.source: The neighbour which dog barks all night has moved out.
exercises.prompt: Corrige la phrase.

accepted: The neighbour whose dog barks all night has moved out

hints: Il s'agit d'une possession, pas d'une chose.

exercises.prompt: She works for a charity ___ office is near the docks.

accepted: whose

fields.regle: Une relative entre virgules ajoute une information non essentielle. On ne peut alors ni employer that, ni omettre le relatif : « My brother, who lives in Leeds, is a nurse. »

exercises.prompt: Ajoute l'information entre virgules : My sister is a vet. She lives in Bath.

accepted: My sister, who lives in Bath, is a vet

exercises.prompt: Ajoute l'information entre virgules : The Clifton bridge attracts thousands of visitors. It opened in 1864.

accepted: The Clifton bridge, which opened in 1864, attracts thousands of visitors

hints: Une chose déjà identifiée : which, jamais that.

exercises.prompt: Ajoute l'information entre virgules : Anna has agreed to run the workshop. Her French is excellent.

accepted: Anna, whose French is excellent, has agreed to run the workshop

exercises.prompt: Our head office, ___ moved last year, is now by the water.

accepted: which

exercises.prompt: Tom, ___ I worked with in Leeds, has just joined the board.

accepted: who
whom

exercises.source: We stayed in Bath. It is only twenty minutes away by train.
exercises.prompt: Fais-en une phrase avec une relative entre virgules.

accepted: We stayed in Bath, which is only twenty minutes away by train

hints: Un nom propre est déjà identifié : l'information est accessoire.

exercises.source: My manager, that started in April, is already leaving.
exercises.prompt: Corrige la phrase.

accepted: My manager, who started in April, is already leaving

exercises.prompt: Laquelle est correcte ?

accepted: Bristol, which sits on the Avon, has two cathedrals

distractors: Bristol that sits on the Avon has two cathedrals
Bristol, that sits on the Avon, has two cathedrals
Bristol, sits on the Avon, has two cathedrals

fields.regle: which peut reprendre toute une proposition : « He was late, which annoyed everyone. » Après un quantifieur, on écrit « most of whom », « none of which », « both of which ».

exercises.prompt: Relie avec un which de phrase : He forgot the handover. It made everything harder.

accepted: He forgot the handover, which made everything harder

hints: Ici which reprend tout ce qui précède.

exercises.prompt: Relie : She sent forty invitations. Most of them were ignored.

accepted: She sent forty invitations, most of which were ignored

exercises.prompt: Relie : Twelve people applied. None of them had the right visa.

accepted: Twelve people applied, none of whom had the right visa

exercises.prompt: The pilot ran for six months, ___ nobody had budgeted for.

accepted: which

hints: Le relatif reprend le fait entier.

exercises.prompt: He gave three reasons, none of ___ convinced the board.

accepted: which

exercises.source: The lift broke down again. It is becoming a joke.
exercises.prompt: Fais-en une seule phrase avec which.

accepted: The lift broke down again, which is becoming a joke

exercises.source: She passed the exam, what surprised nobody.
exercises.prompt: Corrige la phrase.

accepted: She passed the exam, which surprised nobody

hints: « what » n'est jamais relatif de phrase.

exercises.prompt: We interviewed eight candidates, two ___ were outstanding.

accepted: of whom

fields.regle: Une participiale abrège une relative : -ing pour le sens actif (« the woman talking to Tom »), participe passé pour le sens passif (« the boy injured in the accident »).

exercises.prompt: Abrège avec une participiale : The man who is waiting at reception is from the agency.

accepted: The man waiting at reception is from the agency

hints: Sens actif : -ing, et le relatif disparaît.

exercises.prompt: Abrège avec une participiale : The documents which were signed last week have been lost.

accepted: The documents signed last week have been lost

exercises.prompt: Abrège avec une participiale : Anyone who wants a laptop should ask IT.

accepted: Anyone wanting a laptop should ask IT

hints: Le verbe de la relative passe en -ing.

exercises.prompt: The team ___ the migration is on the second floor. (run)

accepted: running

exercises.prompt: We are still waiting for the money ___ last year. (promise)

accepted: promised

exercises.source: The woman who is standing by the window works in legal.
exercises.prompt: Abrège la relative.

accepted: The woman standing by the window works in legal

exercises.source: The report writing by the intern is surprisingly good.
exercises.prompt: Corrige la phrase.

accepted: The report written by the intern is surprisingly good

hints: Le rapport est écrit : sens passif.

exercises.prompt: The people ___ in the lobby are here for the town hall.

accepted: sitting
